title: GTM technical proposal templates and risk annex
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

Purpose: This document provides a concise, reusable set of technical proposal templates, an annex for risk reduction language, and a one-page security FAQ for commercial and enterprise opportunities that involve inference and private deployments. It is intended for field sellers, solutions engineers, and deal engineers to accelerate proposal creation and standardize responses to common buyer concerns.

Scope:
- Proposal templates: executive summary, technical appendix, pricing appendix, and appendix for Dedicated/Private deployment options.
- Risk annex: standard mitigation language for latency, availability, data residency, and regulatory controls.
- Security & compliance one-pager: short answers for prospect security teams and buyers.
- Negotiation and SLA checklist: key items to pre-negotiate and fallback language.

1) Executive positioning (one-paragraph openers)

- Business-facing opener: "Redwood Inference delivers predictable, production-grade LLM serving with transparent unit economics — enabling product teams to ship conversational features with consistent latency, cost, and reliability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- Technical-facing opener: "A unified inference runtime, intelligent routing, and workload-aware batching let your team run the same model stacks across cloud and on-prem with observability, KV caching, and quantization controls to meet latency and cost targets."

2) Template: Executive Summary (2–3 short bullets + 1 table)

Intro: One-line problem statement for the customer and Redwood value proposition.

Bullets:
- Deployment modes: Hosted API / Dedicated capacity / Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Outcomes: Latency SLOs, cost-per-1k-token baseline, and rollout plan.

Key delivery commitments table (example):
- SLO Type | Target | Measurement & Reporting
- Availability | 99.9% monthly | Uptime measured by Redwood console metrics and audited weekly
- P95 latency (generation) | <= 450 ms | Measured at ingress point with synthetic traces
- Model drift monitoring | Monthly alerts | Quality regressions flagged against baseline prompt set

3) Template: Technical Appendix (sections to include)

- Architecture diagram (text description): Model variants behind a routing layer; autoscaling pools (GPU types), KV cache layer, deployment zones, and fallback model policy.
- Networking & connectivity: VPC peering, private link, IP allowlist, egress rules.
- Data handling: request/response retention policy, encryption in transit (TLS1.2+), encryption at rest (KMS integration).
- Operational runbook: escalation path, on-call contacts, runbook links, and access roles.
- Integration sample: concise curl/SDK example showing authentication, streaming, and function/tool call pattern.

4) Template: Pricing Appendix (guidance + two example scenarios)

Guidance for structuring commercial proposals:
- Hosted: per-token generation and per-embedding rates + overage bands.
- Dedicated: committed GPU-hours or vGPU pools with tiered volume discounts and burst allowances.
- Private: platform fee + per-instance support/maintenance + optional professional services for onboarding.

Example scenarios (summary):
- Pilot (low volume): 3-month hosted pilot, capped monthly spend $20k, escalation to Dedicated after 90 days if 95th percentile QPS > threshold.
- Enterprise (high throughput): 12-month Dedicated contract, 2x reserved throughput, 15% volume discount, 1-month warm-up credits, and a canary rollout window.

Negotiation anchors to protect margin:
- Define measurement points (ingress vs egress) explicitly.
- Cap credits and include a one-time migration assistance credit (not recurring consumption discount).
- Keep quantization/throughput tuning as a paid professional services line when large model changes required.

5) Risk Annex (standard clauses and mitigations)

- Latency variance: Provide a measurable latency SLO with a defined measurement methodology; propose an agreed synthetic benchmark harness and a joint tuning plan.
- Capacity exhaustion: Commitment to burst capacity policy with a defined throttling/fallback model family and RTO for capacity addition.
- Quality regression: Contractual checkpoint: pre-rollout evaluation set + automated regression alerts; rollback policy included.
- Data residency: Option for region-restricted hosting or Private deployment with KMS/HSM integration; explicit data deletion SLA.
- Security incidents: Notification timeline (24-hour initial notification), root-cause report within 14 days, and remediation plan.

6) Security & compliance one-pager (Q&A for prospect security teams)

Q: Where is customer data stored and for how long?
A: Hosted: request/response logs are retained for up to 30 days by default and can be configured down to 0 days. Dedicated/Private: retention controlled by customer configuration; by default, we do not retain persistent request logs beyond operational telemetry. All storage options support KMS-managed encryption.

Q: How do you isolate tenant workloads?
A: Multi-tenant isolation is implemented at the process and networking level in Hosted. Dedicated provides isolated GPU pools and network segmentation; Private deployments run in your VPC with customer-managed network controls.

Q: Do you support customer KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. Redwood supports cloud KMS integrations and vendor HSM integrations for Private installations.

Q: What is Redwood's approach to model safety and PII?
A: We recommend prompt-level filtering, PII redaction at the ingestion layer, and post-response classifiers. We also offer an eval-driven quality guardrail that flags regressions on customer prompt sets.

Q: Can you provide SOC2/ISO/GDPR evidence?
A: We maintain SOC2 Type II and ISO-27001 certifications; we provide standard artifacts (SOC2 report, ISO attestation) under NDA and have GDPR Data Processing Annex templates included in the contract attachments.

7) Competitive brief (one-paragraph summary + 3 quick differentiation bullets)

Short brief: Buyers commonly evaluate Redwood against hyperscaler managed endpoints and single-purpose inference vendors. Redwood’s product differentiator is the unified runtime and operational controls that translate into predictable unit economics and deployment flexibility for enterprise product teams.

Key differentiators to call out in deals:
- Unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private reduces integration drag and accelerates rollout compared to multi-vendor stacks.
- Cost controls: automatic batching, KV-caching, and quantization recommendations reduce per-token cost while retaining control over latency SLOs.
- Reliability and graceful degradation: automated fallback policies and regional routing keep services available during capacity events.

8) Case study snapshot (one-page template)

Include: customer profile, problem statement, solution (deployment mode + model choices), metrics (latency improvement, cost reduction, revenue impact), timeline, and contact references. Example metrics to seed: 60% reduction in per-token cost after batching/quantization, P95 latency improvement from 1.2s to 420ms after routing and caching, and production rollout in 8 weeks.

9) SLA negotiation checklist (for deal engineers)

- Pre-define measurement methodology for SLOs and a shared synthetic harness.
- Agree on service credits calculation and cap.
- Define upgrade/rollback and canary windows.
- Establish security evidence delivery timeline and NDA gating.
- Include optional professional services for migration and tuning with time & materials or fixed-fee options.

10) Rapid RFP response blocks (copy/paste-ready)

- "Redwood provides a single API for generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with streaming, function-calls, and structured output support."
- "We support VPC deployment models, KMS/HSM key management, and SOC2/ISO attestation artifacts under NDA."
- "Typical pilot timeline: 2–6 weeks to pilot; 6–12 weeks to production for Dedicated with integration and tuning."

11) Playbook for solutions engineers: how to assemble a proposal quickly

1. Select deployment mode based on data residency and throughput requirements.
2. Populate the Executive Summary table with SLOs and measurement points.
3. Attach the Technical Appendix with network diagram and integration snippet.
4. Choose pricing scenario and include an explicit migration/tuning services line.
5. Add Risk Annex and Security one-pager to address upfront legal/security questions.
6. Send to legal and security reviewers with a 3-business-day turnaround expectation for NDA/redlines.
